One of them was Jürgen Stroop – a war criminal and SS general who had led the infamous destruction of the Warsaw ghetto and was responsible for the murder or capture of more than 56,000 Jews

Photograph: Darko Vojinović/AP View image in fullscreen The wreckage of a Nazi warship has become visible above the exceptionally low water line on the Danube near Prahovo in Serbia this week. Photograph: Darko Vojinović/AP Drought Nazi shipwrecks emerge from the depths as Europe’s Danube dries up Unexploded ordnance and a military motorcycle also recovered following record heat and drought conditions Oliver Holmes Sat 8 Aug 2026 06.55 EDT Last modified on Sat 8 Aug 2026 08.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Record-low water levels in the Danube have exposed remnants of Europe’s Nazi past, with dozens of second world war ships emerging from the riverbed during an intense drought. In the middle of the river on the Serbian and Romanian border, a broken-up hull was visible on a sandbank that is normally underwater. Other vessels were partly submerged, some still believed to be laden with weapons. View image in fullscreen The wreckage of a second world war German warship near Prahovo, Serbia on Tuesday.
